plan.chapterName: Anton, Bivens, and Davis. Calculus, 10th Edition, Figure 15.4.5
plan.contextChunk: This figure contains two panels, (a) and (b), illustrating the extension of Green's Theorem to a multiply connected region with one hole. Panel (a): a blob-shaped region R with a hole; the outer boundary C1 is oriented counterclockwise and the inner boundary C2 surrounding the hole is oriented clockwise, illustrating the positive orientation convention for a multiply connected region. Panel (b): the same region with two horizontal cuts introduced, dividing R into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R''; arrows along the cuts show the opposing orientations (right-pointing on one side, left-pointing on the other) which cancel in the sum, while C1 and C2 retain their original orientations. The figure shows how introducing cuts reduces a multiply connected region to simply connected parts, allowing Green's Theorem to be applied to each piece separately and then combined to give the extended result.

interactionPlan.concept: Green's Theorem extends to a region with a hole by orienting the inner boundary clockwise and introducing canceling cuts that split the region into simply connected pieces.
elements: outer boundary curve C1, thick blue, blob-shaped with counterclockwise arrowheads
inner boundary curve C2, thick blue, irregular closed loop around the white hole with clockwise arrowheads
shaded light-blue region R (panel a) / R' and R'' (panel b)
white hole interior enclosed by C2
label 'C1' above the outer boundary
label 'C2' beside the inner boundary
label 'R' (panel a), labels 'R'' and 'R''' (panel b)
two horizontal cut lines in panel (b) connecting C1 to C2, with opposing black arrows (rightward on the upper cut's lower side / leftward on the lower cut's upper side) showing cancellation
panel labels '(a)' and '(b)'

interactions.teaches: The orientation convention and the cut construction do not depend on the hole's size or position — dragging C2 reshapes R, R', R'' and reroutes the cuts, but C1 stays counterclockwise, C2 stays clockwise, and the cut arrows still cancel

interactions.label: View
interactions.teaches: Introducing two cuts converts the doubly connected region into two simply connected sub-regions R' and R'', each of which satisfies the hypotheses of Green's Theorem

demo_steps.title: Positive orientation with a hole
demo_steps.narration: Panel (a): the outer boundary C1 runs counterclockwise while the inner boundary C2 runs clockwise — the hole's boundary is traversed so the region R always lies to the left of the direction of travel.

demo_steps.title: Introduce the cuts
demo_steps.narration: Switch to panel (b): two cuts join C1 to C2, splitting R into simply connected pieces R' and R''. Each cut is traversed once in each direction, so its contributions cancel in the sum of the two line integrals.

demo_steps.title: Move the hole
demo_steps.narration: Drag C2 to a new position or size: the region, the sub-regions, and the cuts all update, but the orientation convention and the cancellation of the cut integrals are unchanged — the argument is purely topological.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: Because the two cuts are traversed in opposite directions their line integrals cancel, so applying Green's Theorem to the simply connected pieces R' and R'' yields the theorem for the original region with the inner boundary oriented clockwise.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Single canvas showing one panel at a time per the toggle, cross-fading between them. Region fill light blue, boundaries a darker saturated blue with small triangular arrowheads indicating direction (counterclockwise on C1, clockwise on C2). Hole interior white. Labels C1, C2, R / R', R'' in italic serif math styling. In panel (b), draw two thin black horizontal cut lines from the outer boundary to the hole with opposing arrowheads near each cut, and label R' above the cuts, R'' below. The hole boundary C2 should be draggable (translate/scale); on drag, recompute the shaded region, re-anchor the cuts horizontally from C1 to C2, and keep arrow directions fixed.
